## The Post-Rebound Question

By the frozen window, the main question for Samsung was no longer whether it could recover from the 2023 trough. The reported numbers already answered that. The question was whether the first-quarter 2026 earnings profile represented a new plateau or an unusually favourable moment inside an AI-memory surge. Samsung's own guidance suggested management was trying to treat it as the former, while still acknowledging that execution at HBM and leading-edge foundry would determine durability. [FY 2025 results](<https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-electronics-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fy-2025-results>), [Q1 2026 results](<https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-electronics-announces-first-quarter-2026-results>)

## HBM4 Had Moved From Hope to Revenue

The most important change in outlook versus the earlier draft was that HBM4 had already crossed from roadmap to revenue. Samsung's February 2026 release said commercial shipment had begun, and first-quarter 2026 results said the Memory business had posted the industry's first mass-product sales of HBM4 and SOCAMM2 for NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform. That allowed the outlook chapter to stop speaking in hypotheticals about whether HBM4 might eventually matter. It already mattered. The open question was scale, not existence. [HBM4 shipment](<https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-ships-industry-first-commercial-hbm4-with-ultimate-performance-for-ai-computing>), [Q1 2026 results](<https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-electronics-announces-first-quarter-2026-results>)

Management's formal commentary supported that reading. In the fourth quarter of 2025 Samsung said the Memory business was on track to begin delivering HBM4 products in the first quarter of 2026 and aimed to re-establish leadership in the high-end HBM market. In the first quarter of 2026 it again said the business would prioritise AI-related products in both DRAM and NAND. The outlook for the next leg of the story therefore ran through mix discipline and customer retention inside AI infrastructure rather than through a broad commodity-memory recovery alone. [FY 2025 results](<https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-electronics-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fy-2025-results>), [Q1 2026 results](<https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-electronics-announces-first-quarter-2026-results>)

## Foundry Needed Commercial Confirmation

On foundry, the outlook remained more conditional. Samsung's third-quarter 2025 results said first-generation 2nm GAA had entered mass production and flagged timely initial operation of Taylor as part of the 2026 agenda. First-quarter 2026 commentary then said the business would continue 1.4nm R&D and pursue large-scale 2nm orders. At Samsung Foundry Forum 2024 the company had already extended the roadmap through SF2Z and later nodes. The company was therefore not short of technical plans. The uncertainty sat in external adoption and the speed of order conversion. [Q3 2025 results](<https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-electronics-announces-third-quarter-2025-results>), [Q1 2026 results](<https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-electronics-announces-first-quarter-2026-results>), [SFF 2024](<https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-showcases-ai-era-vision-and-latest-foundry-technologies-at-sff-2024>)

That uncertainty should not be mistaken for inertia. The Preferred Networks agreement in 2024 showed that Samsung could still win named leading-edge AI work when it bundled process and packaging together. But the outlook remained one of proof through accumulation rather than through a single headline node announcement. [Preferred Networks](<https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-electronics-to-provide-turnkey-semiconductor-solutions-with-2nm-gaa-process-and-2-5d-package-to-preferred-networks>)

## Devices, Displays and Automotive Formed the Secondary Support

On the device side, Samsung's own releases implied a more modest but still useful support case. The company had launched the Galaxy S24 series as the entry point for Galaxy AI, said the family delivered double-digit full-year growth in 2024, and framed the Galaxy S26 cycle around more agentic AI experiences in 2026. Samsung Display remained a parallel support layer, with management continuing to emphasise premium smartphone panels and QD-OLED differentiation. HARMAN and the broader appliances portfolio also remained relevant, not because they could outweigh DS, but because they broadened the cash-flow base and gave Samsung more than one way to monetise AI and electronics demand. [Galaxy S24 launch](<https://news.samsung.com/global/enter-the-new-era-of-mobile-ai-with-samsung-galaxy-s24-series>), [FY 2024 results](<https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-electronics-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fy-2024-results>), [FY 2025 results](<https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-electronics-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fy-2025-results>), [Q1 2026 results](<https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-electronics-announces-first-quarter-2026-results>)

That point became more concrete in fiscal 2025 guidance. Samsung said the DA business would seek growth in business-to-business, direct-to-consumer and subscription areas and would use synergies from the recent FlaktGroup acquisition to drive HVAC growth, while HARMAN would look to expand automotive orders and add ADAS capability. Those were not thesis-defining drivers on their own, but they mattered to the resilience of the non-semiconductor base. [FY 2025 results](<https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-electronics-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fy-2025-results>)

## Capital Allocation Remained Aggressive

Samsung's posture toward investment also shaped the outlook. The company said R&D spending reached a record KRW 37.7 trillion in 2025, following capex of KRW 53.6 trillion in 2024 after KRW 53.1 trillion in 2023. In other words, the rebound had not been purchased by retrenchment. Samsung was still funding memory-node migration, advanced packaging, 2nm process work and adjacent device AI programs simultaneously. [FY 2023 results](<https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-electronics-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fy-2023-results>), [FY 2024 results](<https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-electronics-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fy-2024-results>), [FY 2025 results](<https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-electronics-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fy-2025-results>)

This was important to the valuation debate because it cut both ways. If HBM and AI infrastructure demand stayed structurally strong, Samsung had kept enough capacity, enough process investment and enough organisational breadth to compound the recovery. If the cycle softened or advanced-node orders disappointed, the same spending base would make the downside feel heavier. The outlook was therefore not just a product question. It was also a capital-allocation question.

The clearest checkpoints after the frozen window were therefore observable rather than conceptual: whether HBM remained the dominant mix driver inside DS, whether 2nm orders broadened beyond the small set of disclosed or inferred programs, whether Taylor started on time and whether DX could keep AI-led premiumisation from turning into a margin giveaway. Those were the data points most likely to confirm or weaken the forward case.

The corrected outlook was therefore simpler than the earlier scenario-heavy version. Samsung had already re-entered the highest-value part of the AI memory stack, but it still needed to make that participation durable across successive generations. It had a credible 2nm and packaging story, but still needed broader foundry validation. And it had a device franchise capable of monetising AI branding, though no longer one that could by itself define the group thesis. Through May 23, 2026, that was the most defensible map of the next phase.
